about: Topic map of the AP Human Geography Course and Exam Description (effective fall 2020, unchanged for 2026-27), written in LevlPrep's own words from docs/aphug-research/framework.md. Every topic title is official (Course at a Glance and its printable poster). Objectives and knowledge are our summaries; for 4.9 to 7.8 the essential knowledge was read through a paraphrasing tool and is marked in source. No CED text is reproduced.

ced.title: AP Human Geography Course and Exam Description
ced.edition: Effective Fall 2020 (V.1), 7 units, 68 topics; the June 2026 clarifications touch only front matter, resource links and Progress Check wording
ced.verification: All 68 titles from the Course at a Glance and its printable poster (framework.md section 2); essential knowledge 1.1-4.8 from a direct text extract of the CED, 4.9-7.8 from a paraphrasing parse of the same PDF (needs-author ced-text).

bigIdeas.name: Patterns and Spatial Organization
bigIdeas.summary: How things are arranged in space and why.

bigIdeas.name: Impacts and Interactions
bigIdeas.summary: How people and places affect one another.

bigIdeas.name: Spatial Processes and Societal Change
bigIdeas.summary: How processes unfold across space and change societies.

skillNames.1.A: Describe geographic concepts, processes, models and theories
skillNames.1.B: Explain geographic concepts, processes, models and theories
skillNames.1.C: Compare geographic concepts, processes, models and theories
skillNames.1.D: Describe a concept, process, model or theory in a specified context
skillNames.1.E: Explain the strengths, weaknesses and limitations of models and theories

skillNames.2.A: Describe spatial patterns, networks and relationships
skillNames.2.B: Explain spatial relationships in a specified context or region
skillNames.2.C: Explain the likely outcome of a geographic scenario
skillNames.2.D: Explain the significance of similarities and differences among places, times or regions
skillNames.2.E: Explain how well a model or theory fits different contexts

skillNames.3.A: Identify the data in maps and in quantitative and geospatial sources
skillNames.3.B: Describe spatial patterns and trends in data
skillNames.3.C: Explain patterns and trends in data to draw conclusions
skillNames.3.D: Compare patterns and trends in data
skillNames.3.E: Explain what maps or data imply or illustrate
skillNames.3.F: Explain possible limitations of the data

skillNames.4.A: Identify the content of a visual source (map, image, landscape)
skillNames.4.B: Describe spatial patterns in a visual source
skillNames.4.C: Explain patterns in a visual source to draw conclusions
skillNames.4.E: Explain what a visual source implies or illustrates
skillNames.4.F: Explain possible limitations of a visual source

skillNames.5.A: Identify the scale of analysis in a source
skillNames.5.C: Compare patterns and processes at different scales
skillNames.5.D: Explain how well a model works at different scales

topics.title: Introduction to Maps
objectives: Describe the types of maps, the information they show and how every projection distorts the earth.
knowledge: Reference maps show where things are; thematic maps show a pattern of one topic.
Maps show absolute and relative distance and direction, clustering, dispersal and elevation, and every map chooses what to show.
Every map projection distorts shape, area, distance or direction.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from docs/aphug-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills ours (needs-author topic-skills)

topics.title: Geographic Data
objectives: Identify the kinds of geographic data and the tools that gather and show them.
knowledge: Field data come from organizations and individuals; geospatial tools include GIS, satellite navigation, remote sensing and online mapping.
Written and qualitative sources (field notes, media, travel accounts, policy documents, interviews, landscape analysis, photo interpretation) are data too.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from docs/aphug-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills ours (needs-author topic-skills)

topics.title: The Power of Geographic Data
objectives: Explain how geographic data inform decisions at every scale.
knowledge: Census data and satellite imagery inform personal, business and government decisions at every scale.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from docs/aphug-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills ours (needs-author topic-skills)

topics.title: Spatial Concepts
objectives: Define the spatial concepts geographers use to describe where things are and how they connect.
knowledge: Absolute and relative location, space, place, flows, distance decay, time-space compression and pattern.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from docs/aphug-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills ours (needs-author topic-skills)

topics.title: Human-Environmental Interaction
objectives: Explain how people and the environment shape each other, and the shift from determinism to possibilism.
knowledge: Sustainability, natural resources and land use.
Geographic thought moved from environmental determinism to possibilism.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from docs/aphug-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills ours (needs-author topic-skills)

topics.title: Scales of Analysis
objectives: Explain how a pattern looks and is read differently at global, regional, national and local scales.
knowledge: Scales of analysis are global, regional, national and local.
A pattern can look different, and mean something different, at another scale.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from docs/aphug-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills ours (needs-author topic-skills)

topics.title: Regional Analysis
objectives: Describe the three kinds of region and why regional boundaries are often transitional and contested.
knowledge: Regions rest on shared traits or patterns of activity: formal, functional and perceptual (vernacular).
Regional boundaries are transitional, often contested and overlapping, and regions are studied at local, national and global scales.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from docs/aphug-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills ours (needs-author topic-skills)

units.title: Population and Migration Patterns and Processes

topics.title: Population Distribution
objectives: Explain the physical and human factors that shape where people live, and how they change with scale.
knowledge: Physical and human factors shape population distribution, and which matter most depends on the scale.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from docs/aphug-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills ours (needs-author topic-skills)

topics.title: Consequences of Population Distribution
objectives: Compare arithmetic, physiological and agricultural density and explain what each says about pressure on the land.
knowledge: Arithmetic, physiological and agricultural density measure population against land in different ways.
Distribution and density affect services, society and the environment.
Carrying capacity is how many people an area can support.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from docs/aphug-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills ours (needs-author topic-skills)

topics.title: Population Composition
objectives: Read a population pyramid and explain what it shows about growth, decline and future needs.
knowledge: Age structure and sex ratio describe a population.
Population pyramids show growth, decline and future needs.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from docs/aphug-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills ours (needs-author topic-skills)

topics.title: Population Dynamics
objectives: Explain how fertility, mortality and migration change a population, and compute RNI and doubling time.
knowledge: Fertility, mortality and migration change a population.
The rate of natural increase and doubling time measure growth.
Social, cultural, political and economic forces shape fertility and mortality.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from docs/aphug-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills ours (needs-author topic-skills)

topics.title: The Demographic Transition Model
objectives: Explain the demographic and epidemiological transition models and how well they fit different places.
knowledge: The demographic transition model describes birth and death rates falling in sequence as a society changes (five stages taught).
The epidemiological transition describes the main causes of death shifting from infectious disease to chronic and human-made causes.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from docs/aphug-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills ours (needs-author topic-skills)

topics.title: Malthusian Theory
objectives: Explain Malthus's theory of population and food and its critiques.
knowledge: Malthus argued that population grows faster than food, so checks follow; critics point to technology, falling fertility and the distribution of food.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from docs/aphug-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills ours (needs-author topic-skills)

topics.title: Population Policies
objectives: Explain the intent and effects of pronatalist, antinatalist and immigration policies.
knowledge: Pronatalist, antinatalist and immigration policies try to change a population, with intended and unintended effects.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from docs/aphug-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills ours (needs-author topic-skills)

topics.title: Women and Demographic Change
objectives: Explain how changing roles for women affect fertility, mortality and migration.
knowledge: More education, jobs, health care and contraception for women lower fertility in most places.
Changing roles for women also affect mortality and migration (Ravenstein's laws).
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from docs/aphug-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills ours (needs-author topic-skills)

topics.title: Aging Populations
objectives: Explain the causes of an aging population and its political, social and economic effects.
knowledge: Aging comes from birth rates, death rates and life expectancy.
An aging population has political, social and economic effects, measured in part by the dependency ratio.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from docs/aphug-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills ours (needs-author topic-skills)

topics.title: Causes of Migration
objectives: Explain push and pull factors and the opportunities and obstacles between places.
knowledge: Push and pull factors, and intervening opportunities and obstacles, shape migration.
Causes are cultural, demographic, economic, environmental and political.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from docs/aphug-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills ours (needs-author topic-skills)

topics.title: Forced and Voluntary Migration
objectives: Compare forced and voluntary migration and name their types.
knowledge: Forced migration includes slavery, refugees, internally displaced persons and asylum seekers.
Voluntary migration includes transnational, transhumance, internal, chain, step, guest worker and rural-to-urban moves.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from docs/aphug-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills ours (needs-author topic-skills)

topics.title: Effects of Migration
objectives: Explain the political, economic and cultural effects of migration, past and present.
knowledge: Migration has political, economic and cultural effects on places of origin and destination.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from docs/aphug-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills ours (needs-author topic-skills)

topics.title: Introduction to Culture
objectives: Define culture and cultural traits, and compare cultural relativism with ethnocentrism.
knowledge: Culture is the shared practices, technologies, attitudes and behaviors a group passes on.
Culture traits include food, architecture and land use.
Cultural relativism judges a culture by its own standards; ethnocentrism by one's own.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from docs/aphug-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills ours (needs-author topic-skills)

topics.title: Cultural Landscapes
objectives: Describe the cultural landscape and how attitudes to ethnicity and gender shape space.
knowledge: The cultural landscape combines physical features with farming, industry, religious and linguistic marks, sequent occupance, traditional and postmodern architecture and land use.
Attitudes to ethnicity and gender, ethnic neighborhoods and Indigenous communities and lands shape places.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from docs/aphug-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills ours (needs-author topic-skills)

topics.title: Cultural Patterns
objectives: Explain how regional patterns of language, religion and ethnicity create a sense of place and unite or divide.
knowledge: Regional patterns of language, religion and ethnicity give a sense of place and placemaking.
These patterns act as centripetal and centrifugal forces.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from docs/aphug-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills ours (needs-author topic-skills)

topics.title: Types of Diffusion
objectives: Describe relocation and expansion diffusion and the three kinds of expansion diffusion.
knowledge: Relocation diffusion spreads a trait as people move; expansion diffusion spreads it while it stays in the hearth.
Expansion diffusion is contagious, hierarchical or stimulus.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from docs/aphug-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills ours (needs-author topic-skills)

topics.title: Historical Causes of Diffusion
objectives: Explain how colonialism, imperialism and trade spread culture and created new forms.
knowledge: Local traits meeting global forces create new forms, such as creolization and a lingua franca.
Colonialism, imperialism and trade shaped cultural patterns.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from docs/aphug-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills ours (needs-author topic-skills)

topics.title: Contemporary Causes of Diffusion
objectives: Explain how globalization, media and technology spread culture and drive convergence and divergence.
knowledge: Culture changes through urbanization and globalization, spread by media, technology, politics, economics and social ties.
Communication technology and time-space convergence spread English, threaten Indigenous languages and drive cultural convergence and divergence.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from docs/aphug-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills ours (needs-author topic-skills)

topics.title: Diffusion of Religion and Language
objectives: Explain how languages and religions spread from their hearths, and compare universalizing and ethnic religions.
knowledge: Language families, languages, dialects, religions, ethnic cultures and gender roles spread from hearths, shown on maps, in charts and in toponyms.
Universalizing religions (Christianity, Islam, Buddhism, Sikhism) spread by expansion and relocation; ethnic religions (Hinduism, Judaism) mostly stay near the hearth or spread by relocation.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from docs/aphug-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills ours (needs-author topic-skills)

topics.title: Effects of Diffusion
objectives: Compare acculturation, assimilation, syncretism and multiculturalism.
knowledge: Acculturation, assimilation, syncretism and multiculturalism are effects of diffusion.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from docs/aphug-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills ours (needs-author topic-skills)

topics.title: Introduction to Political Geography
objectives: Define states, nations and nation-states and compare multinational states, multistate nations and stateless nations.
knowledge: Independent states are the basic unit of the political map.
Nations, nation-states, stateless nations, multinational states, multistate nations and autonomous and semiautonomous regions (such as American Indian reservations).
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from docs/aphug-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills ours (needs-author topic-skills)

topics.title: Political Processes
objectives: Explain how sovereignty, self-determination, colonialism and independence movements shaped today's boundaries.
knowledge: Sovereignty, nation-states and self-determination.
Colonialism, imperialism, independence movements and devolution shaped today's boundaries.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from docs/aphug-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills ours (needs-author topic-skills)

topics.title: Political Power and Territoriality
objectives: Explain how power over people, land and resources works, and define territoriality.
knowledge: Power is control over people, land and resources: neocolonialism, shatterbelts, choke points.
Territoriality ties people, culture and economy to land.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from docs/aphug-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills ours (needs-author topic-skills)

topics.title: Defining Political Boundaries
objectives: Identify the six boundary types and the history each records.
knowledge: Boundary types: relict, superimposed, subsequent, antecedent, geometric, consequent.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from docs/aphug-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills ours (needs-author topic-skills)

topics.title: The Function of Political Boundaries
objectives: Explain how boundaries are defined, delimited, demarcated and administered, and the zones of the law of the sea.
knowledge: Boundaries are defined, delimited, demarcated and administered, and are often disputed.
Boundaries can follow cultural, national or economic lines, or be set by demilitarized zones or policy (the Berlin Conference).
UNCLOS sets territorial seas, exclusive economic zones and international waters.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from docs/aphug-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills ours (needs-author topic-skills)

topics.title: Internal Boundaries
objectives: Explain how voting districts, redistricting and gerrymandering affect elections at several scales.
knowledge: Voting districts, redistricting and gerrymandering affect elections at several scales.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from docs/aphug-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills ours (needs-author topic-skills)

topics.title: Forms of Governance
objectives: Compare unitary and federal states and how each spreads or centralizes power.
knowledge: Unitary states concentrate power in the national government; federal states share it with regional governments.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from docs/aphug-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills ours (needs-author topic-skills)

topics.title: Defining Devolutionary Factors
objectives: Explain the physical, cultural, economic and political factors that drive devolution.
knowledge: Devolution factors: physical division, ethnic separatism, ethnic cleansing, terrorism, economic and social problems, irredentism.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from docs/aphug-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills ours (needs-author topic-skills)

topics.title: Challenges to Sovereignty
objectives: Explain how devolution and supranational organizations challenge state sovereignty.
knowledge: Devolution can create autonomous regions (Spain, Belgium, Canada, Nigeria named) or break a state up (Sudan, the former Soviet Union named).
Global problems, economies of scale, trade agreements and alliances drive supranationalism; the UN, NATO, EU, ASEAN, Arctic Council and African Union can limit members' sovereignty.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from docs/aphug-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills ours (needs-author topic-skills) Essential knowledge read through a paraphrasing tool (needs-author ced-text).

topics.title: Consequences of Centrifugal and Centripetal Forces
objectives: Explain the outcomes of centrifugal and centripetal forces for a state.
knowledge: Centrifugal forces can lead to failed states, uneven development, stateless nations and ethnic nationalist movements.
Centripetal forces can lead to ethnonationalism, fairer infrastructure and cultural cohesion.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from docs/aphug-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills ours (needs-author topic-skills) Essential knowledge read through a paraphrasing tool (needs-author ced-text).

units.title: Agriculture and Rural Land-Use Patterns and Processes

topics.title: Introduction to Agriculture
objectives: Explain how climate shapes farming and compare intensive and extensive agriculture.
knowledge: Climate and environment shape farming practices (Mediterranean and tropical named).
Intensive farming (market gardening, plantation, mixed crop and livestock) and extensive farming (shifting cultivation, nomadic herding, ranching).
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from docs/aphug-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills ours (needs-author topic-skills) Essential knowledge read through a paraphrasing tool (needs-author ced-text).

topics.title: Settlement Patterns and Survey Methods
objectives: Describe clustered, dispersed and linear settlement and the three land survey methods.
knowledge: Farming shapes rural settlement: clustered, dispersed, linear.
Survey methods: metes and bounds, township and range, long lot.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from docs/aphug-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills ours (needs-author topic-skills) Essential knowledge read through a paraphrasing tool (needs-author ced-text).

topics.title: Agricultural Origins and Diffusions
objectives: Explain where farming began and how the Columbian Exchange spread plants and animals.
knowledge: Hearths of domestication include the Fertile Crescent, the Indus River valley, Southeast Asia and Central America.
The Columbian Exchange and agricultural revolutions spread plants and animals.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from docs/aphug-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills ours (needs-author topic-skills) Essential knowledge read through a paraphrasing tool (needs-author ced-text).

topics.title: The Second Agricultural Revolution
objectives: Explain how the Second Agricultural Revolution changed food supply, diets and work.
knowledge: New technology raised food output, improved diets and lengthened lives, and freed labor for factories.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from docs/aphug-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills ours (needs-author topic-skills) Essential knowledge read through a paraphrasing tool (needs-author ced-text).

topics.title: The Green Revolution
objectives: Explain the Green Revolution's technologies and its positive and negative effects.
knowledge: High-yield seeds, more chemical fertilizer and pesticide, and mechanization.
Positive and negative effects on people and the environment.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from docs/aphug-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills ours (needs-author topic-skills) Essential knowledge read through a paraphrasing tool (needs-author ced-text).

topics.title: Agricultural Production Regions
objectives: Compare subsistence and commercial farming and explain bid-rent theory's role in land use.
knowledge: Subsistence versus commercial agriculture (monocropping, monoculture).
Land cost and bid-rent theory help explain where farming is intensive or extensive.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from docs/aphug-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills ours (needs-author topic-skills) Essential knowledge read through a paraphrasing tool (needs-author ced-text).

topics.title: Spatial Organization of Agriculture
objectives: Explain how large commercial operations, commodity chains and technology reorganize farming.
knowledge: Large commercial operations are replacing family farms.
Commodity chains link production to consumption; technology raises economies of scale and carrying capacity.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from docs/aphug-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills ours (needs-author topic-skills) Essential knowledge read through a paraphrasing tool (needs-author ced-text).

topics.title: Von Thünen Model
objectives: Explain the von Thünen model of rural land use and where real places break its rings.
knowledge: The von Thünen model explains rural land use by the cost of transport to one market.
Specialty farming regions often break the rings.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from docs/aphug-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills ours (needs-author topic-skills) Essential knowledge read through a paraphrasing tool (needs-author ced-text).

topics.title: The Global System of Agriculture
objectives: Explain global supply chains, commodity dependence and what shapes food distribution.
knowledge: Global supply chains; dependence on one or a few export commodities.
Food distribution is shaped by politics, infrastructure and trade.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from docs/aphug-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills ours (needs-author topic-skills) Essential knowledge read through a paraphrasing tool (needs-author ced-text).

topics.title: Consequences of Agricultural Practices
objectives: Explain the environmental and social effects of farming practices.
knowledge: Environmental effects: pollution, land cover change, desertification, salinization, conservation.
Practices that change landscapes: slash and burn, terraces, irrigation, deforestation, draining wetlands, shifting cultivation, pastoral nomadism.
Social effects on diets, women's roles and economic purpose.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from docs/aphug-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills ours (needs-author topic-skills) Essential knowledge read through a paraphrasing tool (needs-author ced-text).

topics.title: Challenges of Contemporary Agriculture
objectives: Explain the debates over biotechnology, food choices and feeding the world.
knowledge: Debates over biotechnology, GMOs and aquaculture.
Food-choice movements: urban farming, community-supported agriculture, organic, value-added specialty crops, fair trade, local food, dietary shifts.
Feeding the world: food insecurity, food deserts, distribution, weather, farmland lost to suburbs.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from docs/aphug-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills ours (needs-author topic-skills) Essential knowledge read through a paraphrasing tool (needs-author ced-text).

topics.title: Women in Agriculture
objectives: Explain how women's roles in food production, distribution and consumption vary by place.
knowledge: Women's roles in producing, distributing and consuming food vary by place and type of farming.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from docs/aphug-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills ours (needs-author topic-skills) Essential knowledge read through a paraphrasing tool (needs-author ced-text).

units.title: Cities and Urban Land-Use Patterns and Processes

topics.title: The Origin and Influences of Urbanization
objectives: Explain how site and situation shape cities, and what drives urbanization.
knowledge: Site and situation shape where cities start, what they do and how they grow.
Transport, communication, population growth, migration, development and policy drive urbanization.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from docs/aphug-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills ours (needs-author topic-skills) Essential knowledge read through a paraphrasing tool (needs-author ced-text).

topics.title: Cities Across the World
objectives: Describe megacities and metacities and explain suburbanization, sprawl and edge cities.
knowledge: Megacities and metacities, more and more in periphery and semiperiphery countries.
Suburbanization, sprawl and decentralization produce edge cities, exurbs and boomburbs.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from docs/aphug-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills ours (needs-author topic-skills) Essential knowledge read through a paraphrasing tool (needs-author ced-text).

topics.title: Cities and Globalization
objectives: Explain how world cities top the urban hierarchy and connect the world economy.
knowledge: World cities top the urban hierarchy and drive globalization; networks of cities link global processes.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from docs/aphug-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills ours (needs-author topic-skills) Essential knowledge read through a paraphrasing tool (needs-author ced-text).

topics.title: The Size and Distribution of Cities
objectives: Explain the rank-size rule, primate cities, the gravity model and central place theory.
knowledge: The rank-size rule, the primate city, the gravity model and Christaller's central place theory.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from docs/aphug-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills ours (needs-author topic-skills) Essential knowledge read through a paraphrasing tool (needs-author ced-text).

topics.title: The Internal Structure of Cities
objectives: Compare the urban models and explain how well each fits a real city.
knowledge: The Burgess concentric zone, Hoyt sector, Harris and Ullman multiple nuclei and galactic city models, bid-rent, and urban models drawn from Latin America, Southeast Asia and Africa.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from docs/aphug-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills ours (needs-author topic-skills) Essential knowledge read through a paraphrasing tool (needs-author ced-text).

topics.title: Density and Land Use
objectives: Explain how housing and land use reflect culture, technology and cycles of development.
knowledge: Housing and land use reflect and shape culture, technology and cycles of development, including infilling.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from docs/aphug-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills ours (needs-author topic-skills) Essential knowledge read through a paraphrasing tool (needs-author ced-text).

topics.title: Infrastructure
objectives: Explain how the location and quality of infrastructure shape development.
knowledge: The location and quality of infrastructure shape patterns of economic and social development.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from docs/aphug-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills ours (needs-author topic-skills) Essential knowledge read through a paraphrasing tool (needs-author ced-text).

topics.title: Urban Sustainability
objectives: Explain smart growth and the praise and criticism it draws.
knowledge: Mixed use, walkability, transit-oriented development and smart growth (New Urbanism, greenbelts, slow-growth cities).
Praise (less sprawl, walkability, housing choice, livability) and criticism (higher housing costs, possible de facto segregation, loss of historic character).
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from docs/aphug-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills ours (needs-author topic-skills) Essential knowledge read through a paraphrasing tool (needs-author ced-text).

topics.title: Urban Data
objectives: Compare what quantitative and qualitative data show about urban change.
knowledge: Quantitative census and survey data on urban population; qualitative field studies and narratives on attitudes to change.

topics.title: Challenges of Urban Changes
objectives: Explain housing discrimination, urban renewal and gentrification and their effects.
knowledge: Housing problems (redlining, blockbusting, affordability), access to services, crime, environmental injustice, disamenity zones or zones of abandonment.
Squatter settlements and land tenure conflicts; responses such as inclusionary zoning and local food.
Urban renewal and gentrification help and harm; fragmented local government.

topics.title: Challenges of Urban Sustainability
objectives: Explain the environmental problems of cities and the responses to them.
knowledge: Sprawl, sanitation, climate change, air and water quality, ecological footprint and energy use.
Responses: regional planning, brownfield cleanup, urban growth boundaries, farmland protection.

units.title: Industrial and Economic Development Patterns and Processes

topics.title: The Industrial Revolution
objectives: Explain how industrialization began and changed food supply, cities, classes and the search for resources.
knowledge: Industrialization came from new technology plus resources; it raised food output and population and drew workers to urban factories, with new class structures.
The search for raw materials and markets fed colonialism and imperialism.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from docs/aphug-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills ours (needs-author topic-skills) Essential knowledge read through a paraphrasing tool (needs-author ced-text).

topics.title: Economic Sectors and Patterns
objectives: Describe the economic sectors and explain what decides where factories locate.
knowledge: Primary, secondary, tertiary, quaternary and quinary sectors.
Manufacturing location depends on labor, transport (shipping containers), break-of-bulk points, least cost theory, markets and resources; core, semiperiphery and periphery.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from docs/aphug-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills ours (needs-author topic-skills) Essential knowledge read through a paraphrasing tool (needs-author ced-text).

topics.title: Measures of Development
objectives: Explain the measures of development and what each shows and hides.
knowledge: GDP, GNP and GNI per capita; the formal and informal sectors; income distribution; fertility, infant mortality, access to health care, energy use and literacy.
The Gender Inequality Index (reproductive health, empowerment, labor participation); the Human Development Index as a composite.

topics.title: Women and Economic Development
objectives: Explain how women's roles change with development and why microloans matter.
knowledge: Women's roles change with development; more women work, but without equal pay or opportunity.
Microloans and small businesses.

topics.title: Theories of Development
objectives: Compare Rostow, world system theory, dependency theory and commodity dependence, and their limits.
knowledge: Rostow's stages of economic growth, Wallerstein's world system theory, dependency theory and commodity dependence.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from docs/aphug-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills ours (needs-author topic-skills) Essential knowledge read through a paraphrasing tool (needs-author ced-text).

topics.title: Trade and the World Economy
objectives: Explain complementarity, comparative advantage and how trade agreements and debt link the world economy.
knowledge: Complementarity and comparative advantage.
Neoliberal policy and trading blocs (EU, WTO, Mercosur, OPEC named); tariffs and government initiatives at every scale; debt crises, the IMF and microlending show interdependence.

topics.title: Changes as a Result of the World Economy
objectives: Explain outsourcing, special economic zones, post-Fordism and agglomeration.
knowledge: Outsourcing and restructuring move jobs from the core to newly industrialized countries.
Special economic zones, free-trade zones and export-processing zones; the international division of labor.
Post-Fordism, multiplier effects, economies of scale, agglomeration, just-in-time delivery, growth of services and high tech, growth poles.

topics.title: Sustainable Development
objectives: Explain sustainable development, ecotourism and the UN Sustainable Development Goals.
knowledge: Sustainable development faces resource depletion, mass consumption, pollution and climate change.
Ecotourism; the UN Sustainable Development Goals.

skillsTopics.title: Reading Maps and Data
objectives: Read a map's legend, scale and source, and a table or chart's units, before answering.
knowledge: Read the title, legend, units and source of a map, table or chart first.
Name a pattern with a place: where it is high, where it is low.
Say what a source cannot show.

skillsTopics.title: Scale of Analysis and Map Scale
objectives: Tell scale of analysis apart from map scale and identify each in a source.
knowledge: Map (cartographic) scale is the ratio of map distance to ground distance; a large-scale map shows a small area in detail.
Scale of analysis is the level of the data (global, regional, national, local), not the size of the area drawn.

skillsTopics.title: How FRQs Are Scored and What Each Task Verb Demands
objectives: Know what identify, define, describe, explain, compare and explain the degree each demand.
knowledge: Each of the three free-response questions has seven one-point parts, A to G.
Identify names; describe gives characteristics; explain gives a cause and effect with every link; compare speaks of both sides; explain the degree states a degree, then justifies it.

exam.delivery: Fully digital in Bluebook; free responses typed.

mcq.optionsSource: five (A-E) in the CED sample questions; not confirmed for the digital exam (needs-author mcq-options). Exam forms use five, the bank four (as AP Macroeconomics)
mcq.stimulusShare: about 30-40% with a stimulus (maps, tables, charts, images, text), some in sets

types.none: Q1, no stimulus, parts A-G, one point each
types.one: Q2, one stimulus (data, image or map), parts A-G
types.two: Q3, two stimuli (data, images and/or maps), parts A-G

frq.scale: at least two of the three assess analysis across scales (CED; the exam page says at least one)
